literal: Because evil deeds yield evil results, evil deeds must be feared even more than fire.
translation: Since evil deeds produce only evil consequences, one must dread committing evil even more than fire.
modern: தீய செயல்கள் தீமையான விளைவுகளையே தருவதால், தீய செயல்களை நெருப்பை விடவும் அதிகமாக அஞ்ச வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet warns us about the severe consequences of committing evil deeds. The poet compares the danger of evil actions to fire, which is universally feared for its destructive power. While fire can burn a person physically, its damage is immediate and visible. In contrast, evil deeds yield bad consequences that follow a person relentlessly, destroying their inner character and future. Therefore, one must dread committing evil even more than they fear physical fire.
